title: Pre-Analysis — Corrosion-Resistant Doubler and Drain Path Standard for the Aft Lower Shell
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of the titanium inner doubler standard that replaced the interim sealing arrangement, covering the superseded standard, the external patch repairs already installed over the joint and the bulletin whose reason for existing disappears.

sections.objective: Determine what has to happen to the interim sealing standard, to the re-sealing bulletin driving it and to the in-service repairs already installed over the aft lower shell joint before a titanium inner doubler with an open drain path can be released fleet wide. The work order was raised by the aft fuselage design office once the sample returns showed that the interim arrangement was slowing the corrosion rather than stopping it, and it was asked to report before the design freeze.
sections.findings_summary: Five items were confirmed and one of them decided the shape of the release. The interim standard is superseded outright, which is straightforward, but the aircraft that took the interim arrangement carry an external patch repair over the bilge line on a significant part of the fleet, and the patch fastener pattern picks up the same joint land as the new doubler. Removing the doubler from inside without disturbing the patch was shown to be possible only where the patch is the single-row variant. The re-sealing bulletin has no purpose after embodiment and had to be withdrawn rather than left standing, and both illustrated part lists carry item numbers that disappear.
sections.next_steps: Withdraw the re-sealing bulletin at the same time as the new bulletin is issued, rather than letting the two run together. Publish the eddy current inspection of the joint land as a separate bulletin so that aircraft carrying a double-row patch are found before the doubler kit is shipped. Re-issue both illustrated part lists together and add the titanium item to the aft frame figure so the two lists do not disagree.

similarity_seeds: moisture entrapment behind an inner doubler at a fuselage skin joint
external repair patch installed over the bilge line

tasks.title: Trace the sealing standard and the bulletin that drives it
Survey the external patch population over the joint
Assess doubler removal from inside with a patch installed
List the manual content carrying the aluminium item numbers

expected_findings.rationale: The interim sealing standard addresses the same failure mode at the same joint with the same fastener. It cannot stand alongside a titanium doubler with an open drain path, because the two arrangements make opposite assumptions about whether water is kept out or let out.
expected_findings.resolution: Declared superseded on release, with the supersession stated on both dossiers rather than left to the bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The external patch over the bilge line picks up the same joint land as the new doubler. On a double-row patch the doubler cannot be withdrawn from inside without removing the patch, which turns a two-shift job into a structural repair.
expected_findings.resolution: Eddy current inspection of the land published as a separate bulletin so the patch variant is identified before the kit is shipped.

expected_findings.rationale: The re-sealing and drain grommet bulletin exists only to keep the interim arrangement alive. Once the titanium doubler is embodied its instructions describe a configuration that is no longer on the aircraft, and an operator part way through the campaign would be paying twice.
expected_findings.resolution: Withdrawn on the same date as the new bulletin is issued, with a note directing the remaining operators to the doubler campaign.

expected_findings.rationale: The joint figure carries both aluminium doubler items and the sealant call-out. All three change, and the figure is the list the line uses to order the kit.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-issued with the titanium items, the drain grommet and a pre-mod and post-mod split of the item block.

expected_findings.rationale: The sill frame figure lists the same fastener standard for the frame foot and would otherwise show a shorter grip length than the doubler installation needs, which is exactly the kind of disagreement between two figures that produces a wrong kit.
expected_findings.resolution: Grip length note aligned across both figures.

expected_non_findings.reason: Corrosion blend-out on the aft frame lower flange reads as the same subject in the same zones and was returned high by both methods, but it treats frame material and not the skin joint, and the doubler change does not touch the flange it works on.

type_data.conclusion: Validated. The supersession and the bulletin withdrawal were accepted as stated; the patch population drove a separate inspection bulletin.
